newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surcharges ignored by flat Moscow air cargo market.
newsitem.headline: Surcharges ignored by flat Moscow air cargo market.

text.p: Air cargo rates from Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport were flat in the past four weeks, ignoring the impact of a 10 cent fuel surcharge imposed by foreign carriers.
Forwarders said Russian carriers had not yet increased prices or imposed a surcharge.
Rates to Frankfurt from Russia's leading air cargo gateway rose one cent to $1.08 per kg for a 100 kg shipment and one cent to $1.31 to Luxembourg.
Nikolai Belayev, sales manager of EMS Garant Post, a forwarder for Air France, told Reuters that Russian airlines had not increased their cargo rates yet.
"We have heard no word that they plan to increase their rates, but it could be possible," he said.
Market activity had increased in recent weeks despite the fuel surcharges, Blelayev said adding that demand for shipments was very strong and that "the market was very active,".
"It is not clear whether air cargo rates will be go up in December, but airlines officials say rates will fall in January," he said.
Grigori Portenko, sales manager for freight forwarders Logimix, said fuel surcharges were not a tragedy. "We put it on the clients' shoulders. They are tolerating it."
Portenko also said Logimix hoped for good stable demand until the end of the year. "In January a quieter period will begin," he said.
Sergei Rozhdin, Aerotour sales manager, said his company had given up foreign air cargo operations two months ago due to the loss of many traditional clients.
"We carried cargos for Russian traders, but after new customs rules were introduced most of these people stopped making "shuttle" flights to Turkey and China," Rozhdin said.
Aerotour now planned to concentrate on Russian domestic cargo where demand is growing.

"Cargo food shipments to the Far East and northern Russia are promising. We have many orders to ship cargoes by air to Magadan, Norilsk, Anadyr," he said, adding that the company planned to use freighters stopping off on routes between Russia and China. "It may be a good business," he said.
Nadezda Sokolova, sales manager of forwarder Aeroservice, said that after foreign airlines introduced fuel surcharges her company did not change its tariffs.
"As a result we have got a few new clients who had refused to carry their cargoes on foreign airlines," she said.
Last month Aeroservice increased its cargo turnover about 20 percent compared with September, Sokolova said.

Belyaev said EMS Garant Post had substantial press cargo shipments to Europe in recent weeks and Alexander Buchinchik, Burlington Air Express Moscow export supervising manager, also said business to Europe destinations were good.
"We have a lot of cargo turnover there", he said.
Logimix's Portenko said southeast Asian destinations were good during the last four weeks, while Andrey Voronkov, sales manager of Vinlund Air, said shipments to U.S. destinations were very strong.
"We do not feel any changes on the market due to the fuel surcharges," he said.
Rates to three key U.S. destinations -- New York, Miami and San Francisco -- fell one cent to $2.62, one cent to $3.34 and two cents to $3.22 respectively.
Ilya Maslennikov from Eruslan freight forwarders took a different view from the other officials polled by Reuters saying turnover cargo deliveries at Sheremetyevo airport had fallen in recent weeks.
"Many companies prefer to operate their cargo through Helsinki and the Arab Emirates because they see Sheremetyevo's handling fees as very high and the cargo operations are not efficient," he said.
"We try to deliver cargoes from Europe by truck. It is more profitable," he added.
